To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sweet sorghum biomass can be efficiently converted into bioethanol and biomethane by a biorefining process using organosolv pretreatments with EtOH and IPOH.

the organosolv pretreated sweet sorghum biomass can be used for biogas and ethanol production with the highest gasoline equivalent (GE) of 0.250 L/kg, which is higher than that of the untreated biomass.
the organosolv pretreated solid fraction of sweet sorghums can be efficiently utilized to produce ethanol, and the organosolv liquor can be efficiently utilized for biomethane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a biorefining process for sweet sorghum, which can be applied for the production of bioenergy from the stalks.
the efficient production of biofuels and bio-products from the lignocellulose fraction of sweet sorghums.
the production of bioenergy from sweet sorghums using a biorefining approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this newly developed pretreated substrate is highly suitable to produce biomethane and ethanol simultaneously.
the pretreatment using EtOH/IPOAH mixture is an efficient pretreatment process for the biorefining of sweet sorghums.

the pretreatment of sweet sorgham stalks using EtOH/IPOOH (60:20) at 140 ℃ for 30 minutes in the presence of sulfuric acid at a concentration of 1% (w/w) is an efficient and effective pretreatment process for bioenergy production from sweet stalks within a biorefrinery framework.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pretreatment process is highly effective and efficient for the bioconversion of the entire biomass to biogas and ethanol.
this pretreatment is a good alternative for the production of biogas and ethanol from sweet sorghums.
the pretreatment using an aqueous mixture of EtOH and IPOH could be considered as a promising process for the production of bioenergy from sweet sorghums stalks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pretreatment of sweet sorgham stalks can efficiently be conducted within a biorefiney concept for simultaneous production of bioenergy from the liquid and solid fractions of the pretreatment liquor.
the organosolv pretreated sweet sorghum is a promising substrate for biogas and ethanol production, and the pretreatment can be optimized according to the desired products.
the organosolv pretreatments are a good option for bioenergy production from sweet stalks.
